messages.text: Britain's Kartal misses out on maiden WTA 1000 title in Wuhan

metadata.summary: Britain's Sonay Kartal was beaten in a deciding set by Poland's Maja Chwalinska in a pulsating Wuhan Open final.
metadata.content: Sonay Kartal misses out on maiden WTA 1000 title in Wuhan Open final defeat to Maja Chwalinska | Tennis News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Sonay Kartal misses out on maiden WTA 1000 title in Wuhan Open final defeat to Maja Chwalinska Britain's Sonay Kartal missed out on a maiden WTA 1000 title after losing to Maja Chwalinska in the Wuhan Open final; Kartal had won the opening set but French Open runner-up Chwalinska brilliantly fought back to win in three sets Nigel Chiu Sports Journalist @NigelCJourno Sunday 18 October 2026 15:03, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Wuhan Open final between Sonay Kartal and Maja Chwalinska. Britain's Sonay Kartal was beaten in a deciding set by Poland's Maja Chwalinska in a pulsating Wuhan Open final. Kartal led by a set and a break as she looked to become just the second Briton, after Johanna Konta, to win a WTA 1000 title but French Open finalist Chwalinska produced a superb display to fight back and win 2-6 6-4 6-2. Nevertheless, it has still been a remarkable week for Kartal, the best in her career so far, after only returning to the tour earlier this month following a six-month lay-off due to a back injury. metadata.summary: Eugenio Chacarra won the DP World India Championship by two shots with the Spaniard's third victory of the season moving him top of the Race to Dubai standings, above Patrick Reed and Rory McIlroy, with three events remaining.
metadata.content: DP World India Championship: Eugenio Chacarra wins to move top of Race to Dubai standings with Rory McIlroy finishing in a share of 42nd place | Golf News | Sky Sports Skip to main content DP World India Championship: Eugenio Chacarra wins to move top of Race to Dubai standings with Rory McIlroy finishing in a share of 42nd place Eugenio Chacarra completes third win of DP World Tour season with victory in Delhi; Rory McIlroy shoots two-over final-round as he finishes joint-42nd and slips to third in Race to Dubai; watch Genesis Championship live on Sky Sports from 4am Thursday Sunday 18 October 2026 14:34, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from day four of the DP World India Championship. Eugenio Chacarra won the DP World India Championship by two shots with the Spaniard's third victory of the season moving him top of the Race to Dubai standings, above Patrick Reed and Rory McIlroy, with three events remaining. Chacarra carded a two-under final-round of 70 in New Delhi to reach 21 under as he followed his back-to-back triumphs in June at the KLM Open in Amsterdam and the Italian Open in Turin with another success and secured a fourth DP World Tour title overall having clamed his maiden win at the Hero Indian Open in 2025. messages.text: Van Gerwen suffers another early exit as Van Veen makes history

metadata.summary: Dutch favourite Michael van Gerwen suffered a shock second-round exit at the Dutch Darts Championship on Saturday, losing 6-5 to Irishman William O'Connor.
metadata.content: Dutch Darts Championship: Michael van Gerwen suffers another early exit as Gian van Veen makes history and Gerwyn Price triumphs on return | Darts News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Dutch Darts Championship: Michael van Gerwen suffers another early exit as Gian van Veen makes history and Gerwyn Price triumphs on return Michael van Gerwen's poor form in 2026 continues as he suffers second-round Dutch Darts Championship defeat to Williams O'Connor; Gerwyn Price, Gian van Veen, Stephen Bunting, Nathan Aspinall each progress; watch Grand Slam of Darts live on Sky Sports from November 14-22 Sunday 18 October 2026 01:06, UK Image: Michael van Gerwen suffered another early tournament exit in 2026 at the Dutch Darts Championship Dutch favourite Michael van Gerwen suffered a shock second-round exit at the Dutch Darts Championship on Saturday, losing 6-5 to Irishman William O'Connor. The defeat extends Van Gerwen's poor run of form, having lost his opening match at four European Tour events this season before arriving in Maastricht: the European Darts Trophy, German Darts Grand Prix, Flanders Darts Trophy and Swiss Darts Trophy. It marks his most first-round exits in a single season since the tour began in 2012. O'Connor produced a superb display, firing in three ton-plus checkouts of 136, 131 and 121 to seal his victory and book his place in round three.
